related_questions.question: How much is OPM health insurance 2025 for retirees?

text_blocks.snippet: For 2025, the average cost of health insurance premiums for federal retirees under the Federal Employees Health Benefits (FEHB) program is increasing. The overall average increase for FEHB is 11.2%. For annuitants, the biweekly premiums for Self Only, Self Plus One, and Self and Family enrollments with a government contribution are projected to be $414.00, $902.78, and $991.99, respectively. The government contribution towards these premiums is also increasing, with an average increase of 10.1%.

list.snippet: Overall Premium Increase: The average increase in FEHB premiums for 2025 is 11.2%.
Government Contribution: The average increase in the government's contribution towards premiums is 10.1%.
Biweekly Premium Examples:
Self Only: $414.00
Self Plus One: $902.78
Self and Family: $991.99
Medicare Considerations: If a retiree has Medicare Parts A and B as their primary coverage, some plans may waive the copay for primary care visits.

FEGLI: The FEGLI (Federal Employees' Group Life Insurance) program has separate premium rates, with costs varying by age group and coverage amount. For example, for those 65 and over, coverage may be free with certain conditions, while it can cost $0.867 per $1,000 of coverage for those aged 60-64.

text_blocks.snippet: Federal Employees Retirement System (FERS) employees can generally continue their Federal Employees Health Benefits (FEHB) coverage into retirement if they meet specific requirements. To keep FEHB, you need to retire on an immediate annuity and have been enrolled in FEHB for a certain period before retirement.
snippet_highlighted_words: employees can generally continue their Federal Employees Health Benefits (FEHB) coverage into retirement if they meet specific requirements

text_blocks.snippet: Eligibility for Continuing FEHB in Retirement:

list.title: Immediate Annuity:
list.snippet: You must retire on an annuity that begins no later than one month after your separation from service.

list.title: Continuous Enrollment:
list.snippet: You must have been continuously enrolled in any FEHB plan for at least five years immediately before your retirement date. If your total federal service is less than five years, you must have been enrolled since your first opportunity to enroll.

list.title: FERS Minimum Retirement Age (MRA) + 10:
list.snippet: If you retire under the FERS MRA + 10 provision, your health and life insurance coverage may be suspended until your annuity begins, even if postponed.

list.title: Spouse's Coverage:
list.snippet: If your spouse is covered under your FEHB plan, they can continue coverage after your death.

list.title: Premium Payments:
list.snippet: While the government continues to pay a portion of the premium, you will pay the remaining portion from your annuity payments.

list.title: Medicare:
list.snippet: You may also be eligible for Medicare benefits in retirement and can coordinate it with your FEHB plan.

list.title: Open Season:
list.snippet: You can make changes to your FEHB plan during the annual Open Season, even in retirement.
